item.content:encoded:
"We grow with the world and for the world": PM Modi highlights startup growth, digital innovation Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday highlighted India's digital ecosystem and the role of technology in promoting inclusion, citing the country's digital payment platform as an example of how businesses of different scales can access the same system. ANI | Updated: 13-10-2026 11:13 IST | Created: 13-10-2026 11:13 IST

Prime Minister Narendra Modi (Photo/DD). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

India

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday highlighted India's digital ecosystem and the role of technology in promoting inclusion, citing the country's digital payment platform as an example of how businesses of different scales can access the same system. "We do not grow at anyone's cost. We grow with the world and for the world," the PM said while addressing a gathering at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum. PM Modi described India as the “Mother of Democracy” while highlighting its linguistic diversity, media landscape and growing social media user base as examples of the country's openness to different perspectives. “India is the Mother of Democracy. India has over 100 languages, around 80,000 registered newspapers and publications, and more than 1,000 satellite television channels,” the Prime Minister said. Highlighting India's digital reach, PM Modi said the country had more than 500 million YouTube users and over 500 million Instagram users. He added that people in India openly debated issues and discussed different perspectives, with digital power playing a significant role in facilitating these exchanges. Inviting international delegates to experience India's digital payment ecosystem, the Prime Minister encouraged them to try the country's digital payment facilities. “I would tell the guests who have come from abroad to try India's digital payment ecosystem,” PM Modi said. Explaining how the system accommodates businesses of different sizes, Pm Modi said a street vendor and a car showroom operator, despite differences in their businesses and scale of operations, could use the same digital payment platform in India. “In our country, a street vendor and a car showroom have different kinds of businesses and operate at different scales, but in India, both use the same digital payment platform,” he said. Emphasising the importance of making technology accessible across economic segments, the Prime Minister said, “This is the power of inclusive technology.” PM Modi remarks highlighted India's approach to using digital infrastructure to expand access to technology and payment services for businesses of varying sizes. Prime Minister also highlighted India's growth in startups and digital innovation, stating that the number of startups in the country has increased from a few hundred before 2014 to over 2.5 lakh. PM Modi said opportunities for innovation were reaching more people, with nearly half of startups coming from small cities and towns and 45 per cent having a woman director or partner. “Before 2014, there were only a few hundred startups in India; now, their number in the country has exceeded 2.5 lakh,” the Prime Minister said. Highlighting the growing participation of people from different regions and backgrounds in the startup ecosystem, PM Modi said, “Nearly half of the startups come from small cities and towns. 45% of startups have a woman director or partner.” “In other words, opportunities for innovation are reaching more people, and more talents are emerging,” he added. The Prime Minister said India was also sharing its experience with Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) with other countries to help them develop digital systems suited to their needs. “We are sharing our experience with Digital Public Infrastructure with other countries so that they can develop their digital systems according to their needs,” PM Modi said. Referring to India's digital initiatives during the COVID-19 pandemic, PM Modi said the country had developed the CoWIN platform as an open-source system. He said India's capabilities should help create opportunities for other countries as well. “During COVID-19, we also created the CoWIN platform, which was open source. Our continuous efforts are aimed at ensuring that India’s capabilities open new doors of possibility for other countries as well. In other words, our capabilities should empower humanity,” he said. Emphasising the wider significance of innovation, PM Modi said turning ideas into products and problems into solutions was an important capability, but its impact increased when more people had access to such opportunities. “Friends, the power of innovation is also like this. Turning an idea into a product and a problem into a solution is a great capability in itself. But when more and more people in society get this opportunity, the balance of power is maintained, and its impact increases manifold,” the Prime Minister said. PM Modi also highlighted the role of technology in improving the delivery of government assistance, saying it had enabled direct transfers to beneficiaries' bank accounts. “Using technology, we have created a system to transfer government assistance directly to the bank accounts of beneficiaries,” he said. The Prime Minister added that the system had helped reduce corruption, improved convenience for citizens, and established a direct channel between the government and the people. The eighth edition of the Bloomberg New Economy Forum (the “Forum”), hosted in India, convenes more than 500 of the world’s most influential public and private sector leaders. Under the theme “A World in Play: Defining the New Levers of Power”, delegates will examine the changing state of geopolitics, identify the risks and opportunities presented by this period of uncertainty, exchange ideas, and collaborate on a roadmap toward future prosperity. (ANI)

“World gives thumbs up to Indian economy under PM Modi”: BJP hails IMF's projection, slams Rahul Gandhi as “agent of chaos” Taking to X, BJP leader Pradeep Bhandari wrote, “IMF projects India to be the fastest-growing economy! This is why Anarchist Rahul Gandhi wants to destabilise the established Democratic Order; he is an agent of chaos! Rahul Gandhi hates progress & economic growth!” ANI | Updated: 13-10-2026 11:02 IST | Created: 13-10-2026 11:02 IST

International Monetary Fund (IMF) logo is seen outside the headquarters building in Washington, US (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

India

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Pradeep Bhandari on Tuesday welcomed the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) projection that India will be the fastest-growing major economy, and used the occasion to target Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. Taking to X, Bhandari wrote, “IMF projects India to be the fastest-growing economy! This is why Anarchist Rahul Gandhi wants to destabilise established Democratic Order; he is an agent of chaos! Rahul Gandhi hates progress & economic growth!” In another post, he said, “The world gives thumbs up to Indian economy under PM @narendramodi which has lifted 20 crore+ people out of poverty!” His remarks come after the IMF projected the Indian economy to grow by 7 per cent in both FY27 and FY28, even as it warned that the resilience of the global economy is becoming increasingly fragile amid higher energy and food prices and geopolitical uncertainty. “The global economy remains resilient, but that resilience is becoming more fragile and more uneven,” the IMF said in its October 2026 World Economic Outlook, projecting global growth at 3.1 per cent in 2026 and 3.4 per cent in 2027. The Fund expects global inflation to rise to 4.7 per cent in 2026, driven largely by higher energy and food prices, before easing to 4.1 per cent in 2027. Meanwhile, Congress leader Jairam Ramesh launched a fresh attack on the Narendra Modi-led government over rising inflation, claiming that prices of almost every food item have "crossed all limits". "Vote Theft is the Truth. Back-Breaking Inflation is the Reality," Ramesh posted on X He said that while headlines report retail inflation at 5.54 per cent in September, "the real story is that food inflation has hit 7.74 per cent". He added that the prices of almost every food item have shot up, citing onions (up 108 per cent), garlic (55 per cent), ginger (63 per cent) and lemons (36 per cent). "According to government data, retail inflation has steadily risen from 3.40 per cent in March to 5.54 per cent in September, marking the highest level in 23 months," he added. The former minister asserted that the impact was not limited to food. "The impact of inflation isn't confined to just the dinner plate. Essentials like transportation, education, clothing, shoes, and household goods are all getting more expensive," he said. "The poor are losing their daily bread from their plates, the middle class is seeing their savings vanish from their pockets, and the burden of debt keeps growing, but the Prime Minister is drowned in arrogance, paying no attention to the people's troubles," the Congress leader added. Targeting the Centre over its "achhe din" promise, Ramesh said, "The government that came to power promising 'good days' is not only stealing votes but also robbing savings." "When a vote-stealing government has no fear of the people's anger or losing votes, why would it care about the public? That's exactly what's happening now. Inflation keeps rising, public outrage over vote theft keeps growing, but the Prime Minister sits there like a silent sage. Now it's time for him to pack his bags and go," he said. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
"Power to empower": PM Modi emphasises need to ensure tech progress reaches wider section of society Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday said he had come to the Bloomberg New Economy Forum with the vision of “power to empower”, emphasising that the real question was not who possessed power but how it was being utilised to benefit people.  ANI | Updated: 13-10-2026 10:45 IST | Created: 13-10-2026 10:45 IST

Prime Minister Narendra Modi (Photo/DD-Bloomberg New Economy Forum). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

India

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday said he had come to the Bloomberg New Economy Forum with the vision of “power to empower”, emphasising that the real question was not who possessed power but how it was being utilised to benefit people. Addressing the forum, Modi said technology, data, knowledge and innovation had emerged as sources of power, and stressed the need to use them to create opportunities for millions of people. Welcoming the decision to host the forum in India for the first time, the Prime Minister said Bloomberg founder Michael Bloomberg had chosen the right place at the right time. "Every year at this forum, we discuss economy, energy, etc. For the first time, it’s been held in India. I’d like to say to Mr. Bloomberg that he has chosen the right place at the right time," Modi said. Emphasising the need to ensure that the benefits of technological progress reach a wider section of society, the Prime Minister said the focus should be on how power could be used to empower people rather than remain concentrated among a few. "The right question is: how is this power being utilised? Will technology only be beneficial for a few people or will create opportunities for crores of people? Will knowledge remain the strength of a few people, or empower everyone?" he said. PM Modi said the approach called for a shift in thinking, prioritising empowerment over control, cooperation over competition and helping others succeed over individual success. "This seeds a new thinking — power to empower. Ahead of power to control, power to enable. Ahead of Power to compete, power to cooperate. Ahead of power to succeed, power of helping others to succeed," he said. The Prime Minister further said the idea of using knowledge, money and power for a larger purpose was not new to India, adding that the true value of power lay in how it was used. "This is not new to India. We have always emphasised the importance of utilisation of knowledge, money, and power. The real value of power lies in its purpose," PM Modi said. "Whoever possesses knowledge, wealth, and power, how they use it is crucial. The true value of power lies in its purpose, and it's crucial to understand this philosophy in today's times... Our thousands of years of tradition have taught us this, and in India, we have demonstrated its application in our governance and work culture," he added. The eighth edition of the Bloomberg New Economy Forum (the “Forum”), hosted in India convenea more than 500 of the world’s most influential public and private sector leaders. Under the theme “A World in Play: Defining the New Levers of Power,” delegates will examine the changing state of geopolitics, identify the risks and opportunities presented by this period of uncertainty, exchange ideas and collaborate on a roadmap toward future prosperity. Speaking about the Forum, PM Modi said, “Today, India stands at a defining moment in its journey. India is no longer just a destination for investment; it is a trusted partner in shaping the global future. In our pursuit of Viksit Bharat (Developed India), we are working to build one of the most reliable growth engines of the world and a balanced world economic order. In this context, it is pleasing to note that the Bloomberg New Economy Forum is going to be held in New Delhi in October 2026. The participants in this Forum will get an opportunity to experience the energy of a nation that is not just participating in the new economy, but actively defining it.” (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Germany's fragile coalition hit by labour minister's resignation Reuters | Updated: 12-10-2026 19:48 IST | Created: 12-10-2026 19:48 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Germany's labour minister and co-head of the centre-left Social Democrats (SPD) quit unexpectedly on Monday, adding to uncertainty around Chancellor Friedrich Merz's struggling coalition after bruising state election defeats last month. Baerbel Bas said she was resigning from both positions to deal with grief over her stepdaughter's recent death. She added that "public attacks against me, unfortunately also from within the ranks of our coalition partner," had made her situation unbearable. Bas will be replaced as minister by Alexander Schweitzer, former state premier of the western state of Rhineland-Palatinate, and the whole of the SPD leadership will face re-election in a special party conference at the end of the year. While the departure of one minister was not expected to disrupt the overall government, it highlighted the turmoil facing Europe's largest economy. Merz's coalition has been under growing pressure following state election victories for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) in eastern Germany last month, which it views as the first step towards victory in federal elections due in 2029. Merz's government is languishing in opinion polls amid economic uncertainty and frustration over living costs. Bas, whose former ministry oversees large parts of Germany's welfare system, was the target of repeated criticism from some members of Merz's conservative Christian Democrats (CDU) who accused her of standing in the way of economic reforms. Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil, who shared the leadership of the SPD with Bas, cancelled a planned trip to India and it was unclear whether he would attend a meeting of the Group of 20 finance ministers in Thailand this week. STRAINED RELATIONS Klingbeil said Bas had been subject to "unacceptable" attacks from the CDU while mourning her stepdaughter. But at a press conference, Merz said he had urged his party to show her "every personal consideration, including Christian compassion," in recent weeks. "I cannot see that we have failed to do so in any way," he said, adding that he was confident new minister Schweitzer would swiftly advance pending legislation and cooperate well within government. Merz was speaking after senior CDU members had held a two-day meeting to seek a way forward after months of coalition wrangling over planned tax, pension and labour laws aimed at reviving Germany's sluggish economy. "We want to demonstrate our readiness for change – something that is essential given the election results," he added. As part of the leaders' five-page policy paper aimed at addressing voter discontent, he pledged to push ahead with a cut in electricity tax, reviving a measure that was shelved last year because of budget constraints. While both sides in the coalition agree on the need for reforms to shore up the pension system as the population ages and to help industry confront a surge in energy prices and increasingly intense competition from China, significant differences remain. Merz, a pro-business fiscal conservative, has struggled to win popular support for changes that could push back the retirement age for some, increase the cost of health insurance and weaken worker protections. Support for the government will be further tested in five more regional elections next year that will impact his ability to get major legislation through the Bundesrat, the upper house of parliament filled by Germany's 16 states.
